name: mathlib
summary: Lean and Mathlib environment for formal theorem proving, proof checking, and mathematically rigorous automation.
why_it_matters: Mathlib preserves strong formal-verification capability knowledge, but there is no current validated scenario that needs Vrooli to support it as an active project-level resource.
when_to_use: A future scenario needs formal proof checking or theorem exploration.
Operators want a Lean-based workflow for mathematical verification.
The workflow depends on the Mathlib ecosystem rather than generic symbolic math.

platform_support.notes: The toolchain is portable, but practical support depends on editor, CLI, and package-manager conventions.

implementation_notes: Promotion should validate one or two concrete proof workflows instead of generic theorem-prover support.
Keep editor tooling separate from CLI proof execution.
Do not maintain speculative wrappers when the underlying toolchain already has its own workflow.
operational_notes: Version pinning matters for proof reproducibility.
Validation should run a real Lean check, not only detect binaries.
The core value is correctness, so shallow health checks are not enough.
risks: Formal tools create maintenance load if not tied to an active workflow.
A wrapper can add little value over direct tool usage.
